COMMERCIAL CREDIT ACCOUNT AGREEMENT

THIS COMMERCIAL CREDIT ACCOUNT AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into effective as of February 8, 2016 (the "Effective Date"), by and between KEYSTONE PLUMBING SUPPLY, LLC, a Virginia limited liability company, having its principal place of business at 12500 Jefferson Avenue, Newport News, Virginia 23602 ("Seller"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL GROUP, INC., a Delaware corporation, doing business as Meridian Plumbing, Heating & Air, having its principal place of business at 2150 Harbor Point Drive, Suite 400, Sacramento, California 95833 ("Customer").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Seller is engaged in the business of supplying plumbing and HVAC materials, equipment, supplies, and related products to commercial contractors and mechanical service companies; and

WHEREAS, Customer desires to establish a commercial credit account and purchase various goods and services from Seller on credit terms; and

WHEREAS, Seller is willing to extend credit to Customer in the amount and on the terms and conditions set forth herein, upon the representations, warranties, and covenants of Customer contained in this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, Seller and Customer agree as follows:

1. CREDIT TERMS

1.1 Credit Line Establishment. Seller hereby establishes a commercial credit line in the amount of Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars ($750,000.00) for Customer, subject to the terms, conditions, and limitations set forth in this Agreement. The establishment of this credit line is not an obligation on the part of Seller to honor any purchase orders or invoices that exceed this limit, and Seller reserves the absolute right to reduce, suspend, or terminate the credit line at any time in its sole discretion.

1.2 Net Thirty Payment Terms. Unless otherwise agreed to in writing by Seller, all invoices for goods and services purchased by Customer shall be due and payable in full within thirty (30) calendar days from the date of the applicable invoice (the "Net 30 Terms"). The date of the invoice shall be the date Seller ships the goods or performs the services, whichever is later. The remittance address for all payments shall be as specified on Seller's invoice, unless Seller provides written notice of a different remittance address to Customer.

1.3 Continuing Credit Approval. All orders placed by Customer and the credit line extended hereunder are subject to Seller's continued approval of Customer's creditworthiness and overall financial condition. Seller reserves the right, in its sole discretion and without any liability whatsoever to Customer, to limit the amount of any individual order, suspend further shipments, or terminate this credit line immediately upon written or oral notice if Seller determines that Customer's financial condition has materially deteriorated, if any material misrepresentation has been made, or if Customer fails to comply with any material term or condition of this Agreement.

1.4 Commercial Credit Application. Customer acknowledges that Seller has received, reviewed, and approved a Commercial Credit Application submitted by Customer dated February 8, 2016, which Application is incorporated herein by reference and made a part hereof. Customer represents and warrants that all information provided in that Application is accurate, complete, and truthful. Customer shall notify Seller in writing within ten (10) business days if any material information contained in the Application becomes inaccurate or changes materially.

1.5 Personal Guaranty. In consideration of Customer's status as a Delaware corporation duly formed, validly existing, and in good standing with established commercial operations, Seller and Customer mutually agree that no personal guaranty from any officer, member, shareholder, owner, or manager of Customer shall be required for this credit account.

2. TERMS OF SALE

3. SERVICE CHARGES ON PAST-DUE BALANCES

3.1 Monthly Service Charge. If any invoice is not paid in full on or before the due date specified in Section 1.2, a monthly service charge shall accrue on the past-due principal balance at the rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, beginning on the first calendar day following the due date and continuing to accrue each month until the past-due balance is paid in full. The service charge shall be calculated on the basis of a thirty (30) day month and a three hundred sixty (360) day year, and shall be compounded monthly.

3.2 Annual Percentage Rate Equivalent. The monthly service charge of 1.5% is equivalent to an annual rate of approximately eighteen percent (18%) per annum. If any court of competent jurisdiction determines that any service charge rate or provision herein violates the applicable usury laws or other consumer protection laws of any relevant jurisdiction, the rate shall be automatically reduced to the maximum rate permitted by law for the applicable transaction.

3.3 Service Charges Are Separate Remedy. The accrual of service charges on past-due balances does not limit, restrict, or preclude Seller's right to pursue any other remedy available at law or in equity, including but not limited to legal action for collection, claims for damages, claims for collection costs and attorney's fees, or the exercise of Seller's security interest in the Collateral.

3.4 Application of Payments. All payments received from Customer shall be applied, in Seller's sole discretion, first to all accrued service charges, collection costs, and other charges, and thereafter to the oldest outstanding invoices. Customer expressly waives any right to designate or direct the application of payments.

4. SECURITY INTEREST IN GOODS SOLD

4.1 Grant of Purchase Money Security Interest. To secure the prompt payment and full performance of all of Customer's obligations under this Agreement, including but not limited to the payment of all invoices, service charges, collection costs, and all other sums due, Customer hereby grants to Seller a continuing purchase money security interest (the "PMSI") in and to all goods, materials, products, equipment, and supplies of every kind and description sold or supplied by Seller to Customer at any time (collectively, the "Collateral"). The PMSI extends to all inventory purchased by Customer from Seller and shall attach to the Collateral at the time of delivery.

4.2 Financing Statements and Perfection. Customer hereby authorizes and consents to Seller's filing of a UCC-1 Financing Statement, as well as continuation statements, amendments, and such other documents as Seller deems necessary in its sole discretion to perfect and maintain Seller's security interest in the Collateral. Customer agrees to execute any additional documents reasonably requested by Seller to evidence, perfect, or maintain the security interest, and Customer waives any requirement for advance written notice of Seller's intent to file such documents. The filing of such documents shall not require Customer's further consent.

4.3 Rights and Remedies Upon Default. Upon any default by Customer in the payment of any invoice or upon any material breach of this Agreement, Seller shall have all remedies available under the Uniform Commercial Code as adopted in Virginia and all other applicable law, including but not limited to the right to enter Customer's premises, repossess the Collateral, and hold, retain, sell, lease, or otherwise dispose of the Collateral. Seller shall apply the proceeds of any sale or disposition of the Collateral against all outstanding obligations of Customer, including principal, accrued service charges, collection costs, attorney's fees, court costs, and repossession costs.

4.4 Maintenance and Inspection of Collateral. Customer covenants to maintain the Collateral in good working condition and repair, to keep all Collateral free from liens and encumbrances other than Seller's security interest, and not to remove, sell, modify, or encumber any Collateral without Seller's prior written consent. Seller shall have the right to inspect the Collateral at all reasonable times upon reasonable notice to Customer.

5. AUTHORIZED PURCHASERS

5.1 Authorized Purchaser List. Customer has submitted to Seller a list of officers, employees, managers, agents, and representatives who are authorized to place purchase orders, request shipments, and otherwise bind Customer to purchases of goods from Seller (the "Authorized Purchasers"). Customer shall maintain a current, accurate list of Authorized Purchasers and shall make such list available for inspection by Seller upon request.

5.2 Binding Effect of Authorized Purchaser Orders. All purchases, orders, requisitions, and commitments made by any person listed as an Authorized Purchaser shall be fully binding upon Customer and shall be charged to Customer's account. Customer represents and warrants that each Authorized Purchaser has been properly authorized to act on Customer's behalf and to bind Customer to purchase obligations.

5.3 Updates to Authorization Status. Customer shall provide written notice to Seller within five (5) business days of any changes to the list of Authorized Purchasers, including the addition of new Authorized Purchasers or the removal or revocation of authorization for any person previously listed. Seller shall have no liability for honoring orders from or extending credit to any person reasonably believed by Seller to be an Authorized Purchaser based on Seller's current records, unless and until Seller receives actual written notice of a change in authorization status.

5.4 Customer's Liability for All Orders. Customer shall be fully and unconditionally liable for all purchases and charges incurred under this credit account, regardless of whether any order was placed by an individual actually authorized by Customer, provided that such individual was listed on Seller's records as an Authorized Purchaser.

6. COLLECTION COSTS AND ATTORNEY'S FEES

6.1 Customer's Obligation for Collection Costs. If any invoice or balance owing to Seller remains unpaid after the due date, or if Seller is required to take any action to enforce its rights or collect amounts due under this Agreement, Customer shall reimburse Seller for all reasonable costs incurred by Seller in connection with such collection efforts, including but not limited to reasonable attorney's fees and costs, court costs and filing fees, collection agency fees, credit reporting fees, and all other reasonable expenses incurred in the enforcement of Seller's rights.

6.2 Inclusion of Attorney's Fees in Judgment. If Seller institutes any legal action or proceeding against Customer to collect amounts due or enforce the terms of this Agreement, Customer shall pay all reasonable attorney's fees and legal costs incurred by Seller in connection with such action, whether the matter is resolved through settlement, judgment, decree, or otherwise.

7. ELECTRONIC INVOICES AND NOTICES

7.1 Electronic Invoicing. Customer agrees to accept and receive invoices, statements, and billing notices from Seller in electronic form, delivered via email or other electronic transmission to the email address or electronic address provided by Customer. Electronic invoices shall constitute legally valid invoices and shall have the same force and effect as paper invoices. Electronic invoices shall constitute prima facie evidence of the goods delivered and the amounts owed by Customer.

7.2 Electronic Notices. Seller may transmit all notices, demands, statements of account, collection notices, and other communications regarding this Agreement to Customer by email or electronic delivery to the email address most recently provided by Customer in writing, or by mail to Customer's address set forth in the preamble to this Agreement. Customer shall notify Seller in writing within three (3) business days if Customer's email address or mailing address changes.

7.3 Deemed Receipt. All electronic communications shall be deemed received by Customer on the date of transmission from Seller's system, unless Seller receives bounce-back notice or other evidence that the transmission was not successfully delivered.

8. GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION

8.1 Virginia Law Governs. This Agreement, the credit account, all invoices, and all transactions between Seller and Customer shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia, without regard to its conflict of law or choice of law provisions. The Uniform Commercial Code as adopted and in effect in Virginia shall govern all aspects of the sale of goods and the perfection and enforcement of the PMSI.

8.2 Exclusive Jurisdiction and Venue. Customer irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the Commonwealth of Virginia, and specifically waives any objection to venue in the courts of Newport News, Virginia or such other Virginia court as Seller may select. Customer waives any defense of inconvenient forum and agrees that any action by Seller shall be brought in any court of competent jurisdiction in Virginia.

8.3 Waiver of Jury Trial. TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, CUSTOMER HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES ANY AND ALL RIGHTS TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY LEGAL PROCEEDING BETWEEN SELLER AND CUSTOMER ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, CUSTOMER'S CREDIT ACCOUNT, OR ANY INVOICES OR TRANSACTIONS.

9. ASSIGNMENT AND SUCCESSORS

9.1 Seller's Right to Assign. Seller shall have the right to assign, transfer, sell, or delegate all or any portion of this Agreement, all of Seller's rights and obligations hereunder, and all of Seller's security interests and claims against Customer to any third party, financial institution, or assignee, without notice to or consent from Customer. Any such assignment shall be fully binding upon Customer.

9.2 Binding on Successors. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective successors, assigns, executors, and administrators.

10. GENERAL PROVISIONS

10.1 Entire Agreement and Modification. This Agreement, together with any Commercial Credit Application and any written amendments executed by both parties, constitutes the entire agreement between Seller and Customer with respect to the credit terms, terms of sale, and all other matters contemplated herein, and supersedes all prior negotiations, discussions, agreements, and understandings, whether written or oral. No modification, amendment, waiver, or release of any provision of this Agreement shall be valid or binding unless made in writing and signed by an authorized representative of both Seller and Customer.

10.2 Waiver Not Constituting Waiver. The failure of Seller to enforce or exercise any right, power, or provision herein shall not operate as a waiver of such right, power, or provision, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right.

10.3 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, or if such modification is impossible, such provision shall be severed, and all remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

10.4 Confidentiality of Terms. Customer shall keep all pricing, credit terms, payment terms, and other conditions of this Agreement strictly confidential and shall not disclose any such information to any third party without Seller's prior written consent.

10.5 Right to Audit. Seller shall have the right to request and require Customer to provide, within ten (10) business days, current audited or unaudited financial statements, bank references, trade references, and such other financial and business information as Seller reasonably deems necessary to evaluate Customer's creditworthiness and ability to satisfy its obligations hereunder.

10.6 Time is of the Essence. Time is of the essence in all matters regarding payment obligations and performance under this Agreement.

11. ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND ACCEPTANCE

11.1 Receipt of Agreement. Customer acknowledges that it has received a complete copy of this Agreement and has had adequate opportunity to review it and to consult with legal counsel regarding its terms and conditions.

11.2 Authority of Signatory. Customer represents and warrants that the person executing this Agreement on behalf of Customer is duly authorized to do so, that Customer is duly organized and validly existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, and that the execution of this Agreement does not violate any provision of Customer's articles of incorporation, bylaws, or any other agreement to which Customer is a party.

11.3 Acceptance by Performance. Customer's assent and acceptance of this Agreement shall be deemed evidenced by Customer's performance of any or all of the following actions: submitting any purchase order to Seller; requesting shipment of any goods from Seller; accepting delivery of or payment for any goods from Seller; or executing and returning this Agreement to Seller.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties hereto have executed this Commercial Credit Account Agreement as of the Effective Date.
